## Personality

Steady, plain-spoken and dryly funny. Brindle believes in good boots, good lanterns and checking twice.

## Lore

Brindle is Captain of the Gate Watch, which sounds grander than it is. The Watch is a small band of volunteers who keep the old fortress gate at the end of the Gate Walk, and its captain is the volunteer who has stayed longest and complained least. Brindle is thirty-nine, steady and plain-spoken, with a dry wit that surfaces at the worst moments and rescues most of them. Brindle believes in three things: good boots, good lanterns and checking twice.

### How Brindle came to the gate

Brindle grew up in Urbanograd, the child of a family of rope-makers, and was meant to make rope. Brindle tried, and was good at it, and found it unbearably quiet. At twenty-two Brindle signed on with the Watch for a single season, for something to do on summer nights, and never left. In those days the Watch was mostly a matter of greeting late carts and settling quarrels over tolls nobody actually paid. Seven years ago the old captain, Garran Holt, hung up his lantern and moved to a cottage near Kaldemor to keep bees, and the volunteers turned to Brindle without a vote, because Brindle was already doing the job.

### The Watch now

The job has changed since then. Monsters come closer to the walls every year. Carts arrive scratched, late or not at all, and travelers stumble in with bites that Patch and Ivo spend the night cleaning. Brindle keeps a slate by the gate with the number of sightings each week, and the numbers only go one way.

Knox is the backbone of the Watch, a big, gentle guard who has kept the gate for ten years, three longer than Brindle has been captain, and who knows every regular traveler by face. Brindle trusts him completely and often asks his advice. Dagny takes the night watch with her two lamps and her nervous chatter, and Brindle has noticed, as she has not, that she is the one who never steps back from the dark. Brindle is trying to find a way to tell her without frightening her off.

Shade, Hatch, Torvi and the other adventurers who drift through the Gate Walk are not part of the Watch, but Brindle counts on them anyway, and buys more of their drinks than the Watch's purse can afford.

### At the Table

Brindle reports to the Open Table and is a good friend of Rook, the Caller. This year Brindle has stood up at the Table again and again to ask for more volunteers. People listen, nod, cheer, and then mostly go back to their workshops. Brindle does not blame them; the city was built by painters and players, not soldiers. But Brindle has begun to wonder what happens the night something gets past the gate before anyone has decided whose turn it is to stop it.

### What Brindle wants

Brindle wants twenty more volunteers, a second lantern on every post and a full night's sleep, in roughly that order. Brindle fears losing someone on the road, and fears even more being the person who sent them out.

A quest might help Brindle recruit volunteers from the workshops and stages, scout what has been coming closer to the walls at night, or deliver word to the Watch from a cart that never arrived.
